newsitem.title: AUSTRALIA: TENNIS-SAMPRAS STORMS INTO AUSTRALIAN OPEN FINAL.
newsitem.headline: TENNIS-SAMPRAS STORMS INTO AUSTRALIAN OPEN FINAL.

text.p: World number one Pete Sampras stormed into the final of the Australian Open on Friday with a straight-sets demolition of fifth-seeded Austrian Thomas Muster.
The American top seed, who will meet unseeded Spaniard Carlos Moya in Sunday's final, played at his absolute best to beat Muster 6-1 7-6 6-3 in under two hours.
Muster, the game's supreme baseliner, has won 40 of his 42 career titles on clay and had been hungry for the Australian title to prove he could play on hardcourt surfaces.
But Sampras managed virtually to close the Austrian out of the game, serving powerfully and playing short sliced backhands to break Muster's rhythm and force him forward.

After a lightning first set, lasting only 29 minutes, Muster fought back in the second. He broke Sampras's serve early on and built up a 5-2 lead but Sampras quickly broke back and took a tie-break decider 7-3.

The final set belonged to Sampras from start to finish, although the super-fit Muster never threw in the towel. Sampras missed one match point at 5-2 with Muster serving but won the next game to love.
